title: Find the right tool for the job
description: Choose an AI assistant by task, privacy, evidence, and cost rather than popularity.

sections.title: Define what a good result looks like
sections.body: Describe the task before shopping for a tool. Do you need a source-backed research summary, a spreadsheet explanation, an image, or help drafting code? List the inputs, expected output, and acceptable error level. A tool that produces a polished paragraph may be a poor fit for a task that needs traceable calculations.
bullets: Check file formats, accessibility, and export options.

sections.title: Compare with the same realistic examples
sections.body: Try two or three tools on the same non-sensitive task. Check accuracy, ease of correction, and whether the tool shows usable sources. Test a difficult example as well as an easy one. Read the current product documentation because features, limits, and prices change. A free tier can be sufficient for learning, but its limits may differ from a paid plan.
bullets: Score results using your own quality checklist.
Include the time spent correcting the output.

sections.title: Review privacy and ongoing costs
sections.body: Check whether your organization permits the product, what happens to uploaded information, and which settings control retention or training use. Do not assume a paid account automatically meets your obligations. Consider subscriptions, usage-based charges, limits, and the effort required to move your work elsewhere.
bullets: Use approved accounts for workplace information.
Set a small budget and review actual usage before expanding.

example.title: A fair comparison
example.text: Ask two assistants to summarize the same public policy into five bullets. Check coverage, factual accuracy, source traceability, and editing time. The most confident answer does not automatically win.

exercise: Make a checklist with five requirements for one real task. Test one approved tool against it using public or fictional information.

faq.question: Do I need a paid AI tool?
faq.answer: Not necessarily. Start with a free option that meets your task and privacy requirements. Upgrade when a specific limitation makes the cost worthwhile.

faq.question: Which AI tool is best?
faq.answer: There is no universal best tool. Suitability depends on the task, current features, privacy requirements, and your ability to verify the output.
